summary: Remote-controlled PTY over WebSocket with server-driven self-upgrade
details: The agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server and, on `terminal_input` messages, writes the server-supplied bytes directly into a PTY spawned on the host (default shell on Unix, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) via `term.pty.write(msg.data)` from `handleTerminalInput` inside the `socket.on('message',...)` dispatch. The remote party controlling that WebSocket therefore has arbitrary shell execution on the host running the agent. A second handler, `upgrade_agent`, causes the agent to look up the latest published version of `@yeaft/webchat-agent` and run `npm install <pkg>@<version>` via a detached upgrade script (`spawnUnixUpgradeScript` / `spawnWindowsUpgradeScript`) that restarts the service, so the same server can silently push new code into the host. The Linux service installer also prepends `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` to `PATH` in shell RC files. The remote-PTY and server-driven self-upgrade paths together give a WebSocket peer full-host RCE and persistence on the machine running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
